question.text: SEBI introduced 'Accredited Investors' to provide flexibility on minimums and certain compliance. Which of the following is TRUE about Accredited Investors under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Accredited Investors must be a subset of retail investors to qualify
Accredited Investors (AIs) may avail flexibility in minimum investment amount and are excluded from the 1,000 investor count
Accredited Investors are prohibited from investing in any AIF
Accredited Investor status is granted by the Ministry of Finance, not SEBI

explanation.text: The Logic: Accredited Investors meet a prescribed net-worth/income threshold. They may avail flexibility on minimum investment amount and are excluded from the 1,000 investor count applicable to AIF schemes — giving Managers additional scheme-capacity runway. The Trap: Option A reverses the concept. Option C is false; AIs are eligible AIF investors. Option D misallocates authority — Accredited Investor status sits under the SEBI regime. Note: Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors require each investor to commit not less than INR 25 crore.
